text:
omar: Hey folks - first week question. I'm setting up local dev and trying to follow the secrets onboarding doc. I requested vault access but when I run `vault kv list secret/data/apps/ingest` I get 'permission denied'. Who's the right person to approve for dev read access?

devex-bot: Welcome! New hires should open infra-ops:access with env=dev app=ingest role=read ttl=7d. Include your manager in the ticket. See /confluence/dev/onboarding/secrets.

omar: I opened infra-ops:access ticket INF-1999. I included manager=Tia. Any other fields to add?

tia: @omar thanks - I'll approve dev read. For anything beyond dev (staging/prod) you need app-owner + security. For dev we just need manager ok + reason.

omar: sweet. Also curious about rotation: if I get a temp secret for 7d, do I need to re-run onboarding or can infra auto-renew?

infra: For onboarding TTLs (<=14d) we issue short-lived secrets that do not auto-renew. If you need longer access ask for a service account or approle with constrained policies. Best practice: use vault-mint for service tokens.

omar: got it. One more: I want to run a local job that uses a KMS-wrapped test token. Is KMS unwrap allowed from my laptop?

security-bot: KMS unwrap from personal devices requires disk encryption + MDM enrollment. See policy: /confluence/security/device-policy. For temporary unwraps we prefer to run unwraps on bastion or ephemeral CI runners. If you need a one-off from laptop, provide device proof and request an auditor.

tia: if you only need to validate parsing, we can provide a nullified sample payload (same schema, fake data). Ask infra to attach sample to the ticket and avoid KMS unwrap unless necessary.

omar: thanks. I'll wait for the INF-1999 approval and ask for a sample first. Appreciate it!
